steps.tx: Cytotoxic antineoplastic therapy damages rapidly dividing mucosal epithelium through complex biological cascades. **Oral mucositis** is initiated by **reactive oxygen species** ROS and NF-kappaB activation damaging submucosal vascularity and overlying epithelium following cytotoxic chemotherapy or head/neck irradiation. The five-phase pathogenesis involves initiation with DNA strand breaks, primary damage response signalling, amplification with pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-alpha and IL-1beta, ulceration with bacterial colonisation, and spontaneous healing.

steps.tx: Recombinant growth factors promoting epithelial proliferation protect mucosal barriers during high-dose conditioning. **Palifermin** recombinant human **keratinocyte growth factor** KGF reduces the incidence, duration, and severity of severe oral mucositis in autologous stem cell transplantation for hematologic malignancies. Palifermin binds the fibroblast growth factor receptor 2b on mucosal keratinocytes, stimulating epithelial proliferation, migration, and protective detoxifying enzyme expression.

rows: Dosing & Timing
60 mcg/kg/day IV for 3 days pre-conditioning and 3 days post-ASCT
Stimulates basal keratinocyte stem cell proliferation
Mucositis Impact
Reduces WHO Grade 3/4 mucositis from 98% to 63%
Shortens duration of severe mucositis from 9 to 3 days
Opioid Requirement
Significantly reduces parenteral opioid consumption
Lowers requirement for total parenteral nutrition (TPN)
Approved Indication
High-dose conditioning with TBI for autologous SCT in leukaemia/lymphoma
Contraindicated in solid tumours due to FGFR2b expression

steps.tx: Simple physical cooling during short-lived bolus cytotoxic drug delivery significantly diminishes mucosal injury. **Oral cryotherapy** holding ice chips in the mouth during bolus 5-fluorouracil or high-dose melphalan induces local **vasoconstriction**, significantly reducing oral mucositis. Cryotherapy begins five to ten minutes prior to intravenous bolus infusion and continues for thirty to sixty minutes, reducing peak drug delivery to oral mucosal microvessels.

steps.tx: Preventing chemotherapy-induced alopecia preserves emotional well-being and psychological quality of life during curative treatment. **Scalp cooling** hypothermia devices induce vasoconstriction of scalp microvessels, reducing follicular cytotoxic drug uptake and preventing **chemotherapy-induced alopecia**. Scalp hypothermia also reduces hair follicle cellular metabolism and slows biochemical enzymatic uptake of taxanes and anthracyclines, achieving hair preservation in over fifty percent of treated patients.

rows: Microvascular Vasoconstriction
Reduces blood flow to hair follicles by 20% to 40%
Limits circulating cytotoxic agent delivery
Reduced Metabolic Turnover
Slows follicular cell division and endocytosis
Protects hair matrix keratinocytes from apoptosis
Cap Temperature
Maintained at 18 to 22 deg C scalp skin temperature
Pre-cooling 30 min, during infusion, and 90 min post-infusion
Clinical Hair Preservation
50% to 65% hair preservation in taxane regimens
Contraindicated in haematological malignancies or scalp metastases

steps.tx: Fluoropyrimidine antimetabolites cause dose-limiting cutaneous toxicity localized to palms and soles. Capecitabine and continuous-infusion 5-FU **hand-foot syndrome** palmar-plantar **erythrodysesthesia** presents with progressive painful erythema, swelling, and desquamation, responsive to topical urea creams and dose reduction. Hand-foot syndrome is mediated by accumulation of cytotoxic metabolites and COX-2 upregulation in microvessels subjected to mechanical friction, managed by topical emollients and dose attenuation.

rows: Grade 1
Minimal skin changes or erythema with numbness / dysaesthesia
Maintain dose; apply 10% topical urea cream BID
Grade 2
Painful erythema and swelling affecting ADLs (holding cups, walking)
Hold until Grade 0-1; resume at 75% capecitabine dose
Grade 3
Severe moist desquamation, blistering, bleeding, severe pain
Hold until resolved; resume at 50% dose or discontinue
Prophylaxis
Avoid hot water, tight footwear, repetitive pressure/friction
Daily prophylactic urea-based keratolytic cream

steps.tx: Ovarian vulnerability to cytotoxic damage correlates directly with patient age and alkylating agent exposure. Chemotherapy-induced **premature ovarian insufficiency** POI is age- and dose-dependent, highest with alkylating agents **cyclophosphamide**, causing amenorrhoea and early menopause. Primordial follicles undergo accelerated atresia and direct apoptotic destruction, with women over forty facing an eighty percent risk of permanent amenorrhoea compared to twenty percent in women under thirty.

left.title: High Risk of POI (> 70%)
items: Age > 40 years at time of chemotherapy
Conditioning regimens for haematopoietic stem cell transplantation
CMF or intensive AC-T regimens in older premenopausal women

right.title: Low / Intermediate Risk (< 30%)
items: Concurrent GnRH agonist administration for ovarian suppression

steps.tx: Gonadal damage risk depends largely on the **drug class** rather than a single agent, with **alkylating agents** posing the greatest threat, particularly at higher cumulative doses. In women, **premature ovarian insufficiency** typically presents as amenorrhoea before age 40 alongside raised FSH. Ovarian protection with GnRH agonists may be considered. Men should be offered **sperm banking** before treatment begins, because azoospermia can persist.

steps.tx: Male reproductive toxicity following cytotoxic therapy reflects the heightened susceptibility of actively dividing spermatogonia. Alkylating agents cause permanent testicular **germinal epithelial atrophy** and **azoospermia** with preservation of Leydig cell testosterone production. Spermatogonial stem cells undergo profound apoptotic depletion, leading to elevated follicle-stimulating hormone FSH and absent sperm counts, whereas relatively radioresistant Leydig cells maintain normal masculine secondary characteristics.

steps.tx: Microtubule-stabilizing taxanes produce distinctive nail matrix toxicities requiring protective cryotherapy. Taxane-induced **nail changes** include subungual haemorrhage, **onycholysis**, Beau lines, and painful subungual abscesses, partially prevented by frozen glove application during infusions. Weekly paclitaxel or docetaxel disrupts the actively dividing nail bed epithelium and matrix capillaries, predisposing to secondary bacterial infection with Staphylococcus aureus or Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

rows: Onycholysis
Separation of nail plate from underlying vascular nail bed
Frozen gloves / slippers worn 15 min pre and post infusion
Subungual Haemorrhage
Splinter haemorrhages from fragile capillary disruption
Keep nails clipped short; avoid tight footwear and trauma
Beau Lines

Resolves spontaneously with outward nail plate growth
